title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Goal Setting and Life Planning

questions.prompt: What does the T in SMART stand for?
Grade 11 results are often used for provisional university admission.
Classify each goal.
Rewrite the goal 'I want to do better at school' as a SMART goal.
questions.memo:
✓ Specific subject/target (1)
✓ Measurable mark and method (1)
✓ Time-bound deadline (1)

questions.prompt: Why is a support network important when working towards long-term goals?
questions.memo:
✓ It provides encouragement and motivation (1)
✓ and practical help, advice and information when facing setbacks (1)

questions.prompt: A learner fails a test after studying hard. Describe TWO constructive responses.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): analyse mistakes; ask the teacher for help; adjust study methods; set a new goal; avoid giving up

questions.prompt: A mentor is…
options: an experienced person who guides and advises you

questions.prompt: What is dual protection and why is it recommended?
questions.memo:
✓ Using a condom together with another contraceptive method (1)
✓ It protects against both pregnancy and STIs/HIV (1)

questions.prompt: Within how many hours after possible HIV exposure must PEP be started?
What does U = U mean?
What is the name of the daily pill that reduces the risk of HIV infection for HIV-negative people?
The contraceptive injection protects against STIs.
What is the age of consent for sexual activity in South Africa?
Give THREE strategies for making responsible decisions about sex.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): know your values and boundaries; communicate openly; avoid alcohol/drugs; consider consequences; delay sex; use protection

questions.prompt: Why is regular STI testing important even if a person has no symptoms?
questions.memo:
✓ Many STIs have no early symptoms (1)
✓ Early treatment prevents complications (e.g. infertility) and further spread (1)

questions.prompt: For how many minutes a day should teenagers be physically active?
Which is an economic factor that affects lifestyle choices?
Vapes are harmless because they contain only water vapour.
Which organisation runs a suicide crisis line on 0800 567 567? (abbreviation)
From what age can a person apply for a learner's licence to drive a car?
Classify each influence on lifestyle choices.
Describe how you would set up a personal wellness plan to improve your sleep.
questions.memo:
✓ Set a SMART goal (e.g. 8 hours a night for a month) (1)
✓ Actions: screens off an hour before bed, fixed bedtime, limit caffeine (1)
✓ Track progress and review (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Democracy, Civil Society and the Media

questions.prompt: When journalists expose corruption, the media is acting as a…
Which section of the Constitution protects freedom of expression?
Which organisation campaigned successfully for access to HIV treatment? (abbreviation)
Freedom of expression includes the right to incite imminent violence.
Match each organisation to its focus.
Give THREE ways young people can use social media responsibly.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): check facts before sharing; avoid hate speech and bullying; respect privacy; report harmful content; use it to raise awareness peacefully

questions.prompt: Suggest TWO ways Grade 11 learners can participate in community issues.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): volunteer; join youth councils/forums; start a campaign; attend ward meetings; register to vote
